messages:
Alex G: kicking off network onboarding for LAX GPU cluster (new region). Need NAT/egress path, TGW peering with transit, and private DNS delegation. Will try to keep it low-cost but reliable.
Sanjay P: FYI TGW account id is 123456789012, attachment request created. Need the endpoint subnets for the attachment.
Maria L: I've pushed the private hosted zone for cluster.lax.redwood.internal to Route53. Can someone share VPC IDs so I can create zone associations?
Alex G: VPC IDs: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e (worker), vpc-0f1e2d3c4b (control). Add both to the zone.
Ethan R: For egress, recommendation: use shared transit NAT (transit-nat-proxy) to avoid per-VPC NAT charges. Tradeoff: a bit more latency; but cost saving ~60% at projected traffic.
Zara H: quick cost calc — at 10TB/month NAT GW ~ $900, transit egress via partner ~$350 + proxy infra ~ $120. sounds good.
Sanjay P: routing plan: default route 0.0.0.0/0 in worker RT -> TGW attachment -> transit NAT. We also need a specific route for the datastore CIDR to go direct to control plane.
Alex G: Also need to confirm BGP propagation across TGW for the peer with our colo. Sanjay, can you confirm ASN and BGP session details?
Sanjay P: ASN 64512, BGP peer with colo on 192.0.2.2/30. I started the BGP session from the colo side, sees prefixes from our TGW. All good.
Maria L: DNS: delegated cluster.lax.redwood.internal as a private zone associated to the two VPCs. For external resolvers, we've added conditional forwarding from on-prem to Route53 via the transit resolver.
Zara H: smoke-tests I ran (from a worker pod):
```bash
# check metadata
curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id || true
# check egress
curl -s --connect-timeout 5 https://ifconfig.co || echo "egress-fail"
# dns
nslookup api.cluster.lax.redwood.internal || true
``` 
All returned expected values, except intermittent 504s during NAT failover window.
Ethan R: 504s likely due to connection tracking when we moved between NAT instances. Suggest enabling connection tracking sync or use stateful NAT appliance in the transit path.
Alex G: ops-bot — can you confirm whether the stage autoscaler hit the burst capacity during the window? @ops-bot
ops-bot: autoscaler alert: burst-capacity used 28% between 2134568010 and 2134568035, no pod evictions.
Sanjay P: route table tidbit — remember to add a /32 host route for the colo healthcheck IP to go direct to the control VPC, otherwise healthchecks loop into transit.
deploy-bot: route-table rtb-0c9d8e7f updated: added 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-attachment-0abc1234
Zara H: re: DNS delegation verification: dig from on-prem returned NS records for cluster.lax, good. One outstanding: TTLs are 300, might want 60 for quick rollouts.
Maria L: lowered TTL to 60 for cluster.lax.redwood.internal
Alex G: Next steps: Sanjay to finalize TGW attachment and BGP stability checks; Maria to confirm zone associations + TTL change (done); Ethan to propose NAT failover plan (conntrack sync or appliance); Zara to run 1-day soak and post metrics. I'll hand off to oncall for 48h monitoring.
Sanjay P: on it, will post a short checklist when TGW peering is fully green :thumbsup:
Ethan R: I'll prototype conntrack-sync this afternoon and report back.
Zara H: starting 24h soak now, will log any DNS/egress blips in #eng-infra-monitoring.
Alex G: thanks team. Handoff: @oncall-lax you're on for the next 48h, please watch NAT error rate and egress latency. Ping me for escalation.
